title: Human-in-the-Loop and Approval Flows
description: Add approval gates, escalation rules, and human feedback collection to agent workflows in C# backends.

blocks.text: Not every agent action should execute automatically. Approval flows let humans review high-risk tool calls, correct mistakes, and provide feedback that improves future behavior.

blocks.title: Common patterns
items: **Always-approve** — pause before any side-effecting tool call.
**Risk-based approval** — auto-approve reads, require approval for writes or sends.
**Exception approval** — run freely until an error threshold is exceeded.
**User-initiated review** — let users request a review of recent agent actions.

blocks.title: Conceptual approval decorator
blocks.content: Wrap tool execution with approval checks.

blocks.title: Persist approvals
blocks.text: Store approval decisions with request IDs, timestamps, and approver identity. This creates an audit trail and supports replay or rollback.

items.text: I can classify tool calls by risk level
items.hint: Read-only versus side-effecting; reversible versus destructive

items.text: I persist approval decisions for audit
items.hint: Store approver, timestamp, outcome, and request context

items.text: I provide users with a way to review recent actions
items.hint: History, undo or rollback mechanisms, and feedback collection

blocks.title: Lesson Summary
points: Human-in-the-loop builds trust and reduces risk.
Risk-based approval balances automation with control.
Persist approvals for compliance and debugging.
blocks.takeaway: Agents should be powerful but accountable. Approval flows are the control surface that makes AI features safe for production users.
